question: On 21 July 2026, the Dutch Trade and Industry Appeals Tribunal (CBb), one of the Netherlands’ highest administrative courts, ruled that catching poultry by the legs is prohibited under Regulation (EC) No 1/2005. Dutch operators must discontinue this practice by 1 January 2027, after which non-compliance may result in penalty payments of up to EUR 60 000. The prohibition is not enforced in other Member States.

Moreover, the UK Government concluded that Regulation 1/2005 was not intended to prohibit lifting poultry by the legs and considered the failure to exempt poultry an ’inadvertent drafting error’. The UK consequently amended legislation in 2025 to permit twoleg catching.
The Commission’s proposal for a new Animal Transport Regulation likewise explicitly allows birds to be caught, lifted and carried by both legs under specified conditions. 1.

Does the Commission agree that the current Dutch enforcement, including penalty payments, is inappropriate considering the apparent lack of an original intention to prohibit this practice, the lack of similar enforcement in other Member States, and the Commission’s proposal to explicitly allow this practice?
What action can the Commission take to ensure this enforcement is no longer required, and is it willing to take such action before 1 January 2027?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2026) First, the Commission would like to recall that only the Court of Justice of the European Union is competent to authoritatively interpret EU law. The Commission considers that point 1.8(d) of Chapter III of Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1/20051 does not lay down an absolute prohibition on catching of poultry by the legs.

While recommending catching of poultry by the body where possible, the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) acknowledges that this may not be possible in practice in all cases. If poultry cannot be caught by the body, EFSA recommends the specific measures to be taken when catching poultry by the legs to avoid suffering2.

The primary responsibility for enforcing compliance with EU legislation in the area of animal health and welfare lies with the Member States, while the Commission ensures consistent application across the EU through monitoring and by verifying the functioning of national control systems, and making publicly available the reports of audits in Member States3.

To further strengthen legal certainty, the Commission’s 2023 legislative proposal4 repealing Regulation (EC) No 1/2005 aims to provide greater clarity on the conditions under which this practice may be permitted. The proposal makes it clear that catching poultry by the legs is allowed and details how such catching can be performed5. The proposal is currently being examined by the co-legislators.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 1/2005 of 22 December 2004 on the protection of animals during transport and
related operations and amending Directives 64/432/EEC and 93/119/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1255/97 (OJ L 3, 5.1.2005, p. 1).

2 EFSA Scientific Opinion of 30 June 2022 on the ‘Welfare of domestic birds and rabbits transported in containers’ recommends training of the poultry catchers, and, where birds are caught by the legs, catching, lifting and carrying birds by 2 legs, with maximum 3 birds per hand, and minimising the duration of the inversion.

3 Article 116 and Article 117 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 (the Official Controls Regulation or OCR) empower the European Commission to perform audits in Member States and govern the publication of the resulting reports. 4 COM/2023/770 final. 5 See Point 3.1(d) and 3.7 of Chapter III of Annex I of the 2023 Commission proposal.
